spans.s:
Śauva-udgītha
(‘the उद्गीथ revealed through a dog’)
------------------------------------------
There is an interesting incident mentioned in the Chāndogya Upaniṣad (1.12)
A sage, Glāva-मैत्रेय by name, had started searching for a suitable place to repeat and study the वेदस्. He suddenly saw a beautiful white dog in front of him. Very soon a few more dogs too appeared on the scene and requested the white dog to get them food—because they were hungry—by singing for the same. They were asked to be present in that very place the next morning. And they did so.
Now, as per the directions of the chief dog, they formed a continuous chain—each dog catching hold of the tail of the dog in front of it—and started singing an उद्गीथ (the second, the most important, part of a sāma chanting) which was a prayer addressed to the deity आदित्य (Sun-god) and requesting him for ड़ोओद्.
The dogs had actually imitated such a formation by the priests in a सोमयाग during the chanting of the बहिष्पवमान hymn.
This came to be known as the शौव-उद्गीथ, the उद्गीथ revealed by a dog.
The white dog was a deva (god) or a ṛṣi (sage) in that disguise.
It had appeared before the sage Glāva-मैत्रेय to teach him an उद्गीथ by singing which, one could get plenty of ड़ोओद्. This had become necessary since the people (as per the previous section of the Chāndogya Upaniṣad) were suffering from a famine.
The dogs represent the mukhya or the chief प्राण and the subsidiary prāṇas.
